samples.question: The picture is a single row of cream cards on a plain background. The cards are applied one at a time in drawn left-to-right order, as the grey arrow beneath the row shows. There are exactly two kinds of card and each card is one of them. An ADD card carries one coloured bar standing on the same baseline as every other bar in the picture. That bar is an item: its colour is the item's name and its drawn height above the shared baseline is the item's priority, so a taller bar means a higher priority. No two bars in the picture have the same colour and no two have the same height. A SERVE card carries one black triangle pointing downwards and no bar at all. Apply the cards by this rule. An ADD card puts its item into the waiting group. A SERVE card takes exactly one item out of the waiting group: the item whose bar is the tallest of the bars of all items then waiting, no matter when those items were added. An item that has been taken out is gone and can never be taken out again; an item that is never taken out simply stays waiting. Every SERVE card in this picture has at least two items waiting when it acts, and the last card of the row is a SERVE card. The waiting group is never drawn anywhere: the picture shows only the row of cards, always in their original drawn state, and no card is redrawn or crossed out after it acts. Bar colours come from red, orange, blue, green, purple and teal. After every card has acted in order, which colour of bar did the LAST SERVE card of the row take out of the waiting group? Answer with one word: red, orange, blue, green, purple or teal.
